description: We are a team building an interactive, educational space mission simulator that helps young learners understand the challenges of living on the Moon or Mars. Players will manage resources such as oxygen, water, food, and power while making decisions to keep their astronauts safe.
summary:
Opost is a cross-platform interactive resource-management simulator developed by Team Orbit Builders for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, specifically tailored for kids ages 7–12+. The application lets students manage a lunar or Martian outpost, balancing competing survival demands like life support, power, food production, and radiation shielding.

To bridge the gap between abstract space facts and complex engineering, Opost is grounded in authentic NASA open data. It integrates real-time space weather telemetry from NASA DONKI to simulate radiation risks and NASA OSDR biological research for in-game astronaut health insights.

Opost is vital because it makes real engineering trade-offs tangible and fun. By ensuring no choice is free—such as diverting power for radiation protection during a solar flare—the simulator transforms young learners from passive observers into active mission planners, fostering critical thinking for the future of space exploration.
details:
1. What Opost Does & How It Works

Opost is an interactive, browser-based resource-management simulation game designed specifically for kids ages 7–12+ and students. The app lets players step into the shoes of mission commanders running a 30-Sol lunar or Martian outpost.

  • The Core Loop: Players face the daily challenge of balancing competing survival demands—distributing a limited pool of power across life support, radiation shielding, food production, and scientific exploration.
  • Real-Time NASA Integration: Opost avoids invented statistics by grounding gameplay in authentic NASA open data. It integrates real-time space weather telemetry from NASA DONKI (triggering solar flare and radiation warnings that require immediate shield allocation) and biological research insights from the NASA OSDR (Open Science Data Repository) to present in-game astronaut health and research fact cards.

2. Benefits of the Project

  • Makes Complex Trade-Offs Tangible: Instead of presenting space facts as abstract text or posters, Opost proves that no choice is free. If a player boosts shielding to prepare for a solar storm, energy available for food growth or life support temporarily drops.
  • Low Barrier to Entry: Built as a responsive Progressive Web App (PWA), Opost runs instantly in any browser with zero downloads, logins, or installation required.
  • Kid-Friendly Accessibility: Complex engineering concepts are translated into clean, intuitive HUD elements, sci-fi vector icons, and plain-language tooltips rather than dense jargon.

3. Intended Impact

The primary impact of Opost is to shift young learners from passive observers of space exploration to active, critical-thinking mission planners. By experiencing firsthand the exact constraints and decision-making logic that NASA mission planners navigate daily, students develop a deeper appreciation for STEM, systems engineering, and the realities of deep-space survival, inspiring the next generation of space scientists and innovators.

4. Tech Stack, Tools & Software Used

  • Frontend & UI: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript (Vite-powered environment), and custom glassmorphism styling for an immersive space-tech HUD experience.
  • Data Sources & APIs: NASA Open APIs, including DONKI (Space Weather Database of Notifications, Knowledge, Information), OSDR (Open Science Data Repository), APOD, and Mars Rover Photos.
  • Development & Collaboration: Developed using Lovable for rapid application prototyping, VS Code on Linux/Parrot OS, and Git/GitHub for team version control and collaboration.
  • Deployment & Hosting: Deployed on Netlify/Vercel, optimized for fast loading and cross-platform mobile/desktop responsiveness.

5. Project Creativity & Innovation

Opost is creative because it bridges the gap between pure entertainment and scientific accuracy. While many educational games oversimplify space travel into frictionless fun, Opost introduces genuine mechanical tension. Its innovation lies in transforming live, complex space-weather datasets (DONKI) and biological research (OSDR) into lightweight, gamified mechanics—packaged inside a sleek, collapsible-sidebar spaceship HUD interface that feels like an authentic mission control console.

6. Key Factors Considered by the Team

  • Cognitive Load for Young Learners: We deliberately avoided overwhelming players with 5 or 6 simultaneous variables, focusing instead on core survival metrics (Oxygen, Water, Power, Shielding, and Crew Health) to keep the experience engaging rather than stressful.
  • Meaningful Failure & Replayability: Designing the 30-Sol mission loop to allow failure ensures kids learn from poor resource distribution, encouraging them to retry with new strategies.
  • Data Attribution: Ensuring clear, in-app attribution so players and judges instantly recognize that they are interacting with genuine NASA science and research findings.
dataRefs: NASA Open APIs: NASA's central public API portal, providing free programmatic access to datasets including the Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), Mars Rover Photos, and the Space Weather Database (DONKI). A free API key (higher rate limits than the shared demo key) can be requested instantly and is a good starting point for any challenge team building a data-connected prototype.
